data.claim: A token-exhausted run can be safely resumed iff three conditions jointly hold: (1) clean halt—the final event was fully committed and persisted before the exhaustion signal was raised, so no partial write exists at the log tail; (2) append-only identity integrity—the hash chain (or equivalent identity structure) from genesis to the tail event is verifiable and unbroken; (3) resumption strictly appends new events after the verified tail without mutating, inserting, or reordering any existing event. Resumption must be refused when the tail is a partial or uncommitted write, when the chain is broken, or when any evidence suggests an interrupted commit.
